raw: Act 4, Scene 1 — Friar Lawrence’s Cell
Enter Friar Lawrence and Paris.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: On Thursday, sir? The time is very short.

gemma4_gloss.en: On Thursday, sir?
The time is very short.

speaker: PARIS
raw:
My father Capulet will have it so;
And I am nothing slow to slack his haste.

gemma4_gloss.en: My father Capulet wants it this way.
I am not slow to follow his plan.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
You say you do not know the lady’s mind.
Uneven is the course; I like it not.

gemma4_gloss.en: You say you do not know the lady's mind.
The situation is uncertain.
I do not like it.

speaker: PARIS
raw:
Immoderately she weeps for Tybalt’s death,
And therefore have I little talk’d of love;
For Venus smiles not in a house of tears.
Now, sir, her father counts it dangerous
That she do give her sorrow so much sway;
And in his wisdom, hastes our marriage,
To stop the inundation of her tears,
Which, too much minded by herself alone,
May be put from her by society.
Now do you know the reason of this haste.

gemma4_gloss.en: She cries too much for Tybalt's death.
Therefore, I have hardly talked about love.
Love does not smile in a house of tears.
Now, sir, her father thinks it is dangerous.
He thinks she lets her sadness control her too much.
In his wisdom, he hurries our marriage.
He wants to stop the flow of her tears.
She might stop crying if she spends time with others.
Now do you know the reason for this haste?

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
I would I knew not why it should be slow’d.—
Look, sir, here comes the lady toward my cell.

gemma4_gloss.en: I wish I did not know why it should be delayed.
Look, sir, here comes the lady toward my cell.

raw: Enter Juliet.

speaker: PARIS
raw: Happily met, my lady and my wife!

gemma4_gloss.en: I am happy to meet you, my lady and my wife!

speaker: JULIET
raw: That may be, sir, when I may be a wife.

gemma4_gloss.en: That may be true, sir, when I am a wife.

speaker: PARIS
raw: That may be, must be, love, on Thursday next.

gemma4_gloss.en: That may be, it must be, love, next Thursday.

speaker: JULIET
raw: What must be shall be.

gemma4_gloss.en: What must happen will happen.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: That’s a certain text.

gemma4_gloss.en: That is a certain statement.

speaker: PARIS
raw: Come you to make confession to this father?

gemma4_gloss.en: Do you come to confess to this priest?

speaker: JULIET
raw: To answer that, I should confess to you.

gemma4_gloss.en: To answer that, I would have to confess to you.

speaker: PARIS
raw: Do not deny to him that you love me.

gemma4_gloss.en: Do not deny your love for me to him.

speaker: JULIET
raw: I will confess to you that I love him.

gemma4_gloss.en: I will tell you that I love him.

speaker: PARIS
raw: So will ye, I am sure, that you love me.

gemma4_gloss.en: I am sure you will say that you love me.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
If I do so, it will be of more price,
Being spoke behind your back than to your face.

gemma4_gloss.en: If I do so, it will be more valuable.
It would be said behind your back instead of to your face.

speaker: PARIS
raw: Poor soul, thy face is much abus’d with tears.

gemma4_gloss.en: Poor soul.
Your face is ruined by many tears.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
The tears have got small victory by that;
For it was bad enough before their spite.

gemma4_gloss.en: The tears have not won a small victory over that.
It was already bad enough before their spite.

speaker: PARIS
raw: Thou wrong’st it more than tears with that report.

gemma4_gloss.en: You hurt it more with that report than the tears do.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
That is no slander, sir, which is a truth,
And what I spake, I spake it to my face.

gemma4_gloss.en: That is not slander, sir, because it is the truth.
And I spoke it to your face.

speaker: PARIS
raw: Thy face is mine, and thou hast slander’d it.

gemma4_gloss.en: Your face is mine.
And you have insulted it.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
It may be so, for it is not mine own.
Are you at leisure, holy father, now,
Or shall I come to you at evening mass?

gemma4_gloss.en: It may be so, for it is not my own.
Are you free now, holy father?
Or should I come to you at the evening mass?

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
My leisure serves me, pensive daughter, now.—
My lord, we must entreat the time alone.

gemma4_gloss.en: I am free now, my thoughtful daughter.
My lord, we must talk alone for a moment.

speaker: PARIS
raw:
God shield I should disturb devotion!—
Juliet, on Thursday early will I rouse ye,
Till then, adieu; and keep this holy kiss.

gemma4_gloss.en: God forbid that I should disturb your prayers!
Juliet, I will wake you early on Thursday.
Until then, goodbye.
And keep this holy kiss.

raw: Exit.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O shut the door, and when thou hast done so,
Come weep with me, past hope, past cure, past help!

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh, shut the door.
When you have done that, come and cry with me.
My situation is hopeless.
It cannot be cured.
No one can help me!

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
O Juliet, I already know thy grief;
It strains me past the compass of my wits.
I hear thou must, and nothing may prorogue it,
On Thursday next be married to this County.

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh Juliet, I already know your grief.
It is more than my mind can handle.
I hear that you must marry the Count.
You must do it this coming Thursday.
Nothing can stop it.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Tell me not, Friar, that thou hear’st of this,
Unless thou tell me how I may prevent it.
If in thy wisdom, thou canst give no help,
Do thou but call my resolution wise,
And with this knife I’ll help it presently.
God join’d my heart and Romeo’s, thou our hands;
And ere this hand, by thee to Romeo’s seal’d,
Shall be the label to another deed,
Or my true heart with treacherous revolt
Turn to another, this shall slay them both.
Therefore, out of thy long-experienc’d time,
Give me some present counsel, or behold
’Twixt my extremes and me this bloody knife
Shall play the empire, arbitrating that
Which the commission of thy years and art
Could to no issue of true honour bring.
Be not so long to speak. I long to die,
If what thou speak’st speak not of remedy.

gemma4_gloss.en: Do not tell me about this, Friar, unless you tell me how I can stop it.
If your wisdom gives no help, just call my decision wise.
I will use this knife to help it right now.
God joined my heart and Romeo's.
He joined our hands.
Before this hand is joined to Romeo's, it will be the label for another deed.
Or if my true heart turns to another because of a betrayal, this knife will kill both of them.
Therefore, use your long experience.
Give me some immediate advice.
Look at my two choices.
This bloody knife will decide for me.
Your years and wisdom could not find a way to keep my honor.
Do not take a long time to speak.
I want to die.
Unless what you say offers a cure.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Hold, daughter. I do spy a kind of hope,
Which craves as desperate an execution
As that is desperate which we would prevent.
If, rather than to marry County Paris
Thou hast the strength of will to slay thyself,
Then is it likely thou wilt undertake
A thing like death to chide away this shame,
That cop’st with death himself to scape from it.
And if thou dar’st, I’ll give thee remedy.

gemma4_gloss.en: Wait, daughter.
I see a kind of hope.
It requires a desperate action.
That action is as desperate as the one we want to prevent.
If you have the will to kill yourself instead of marrying Count Paris, then it is likely you will try something like death.
You do this to escape this shame.
You would risk death to avoid it.
And if you dare, I will give you a remedy.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
O, bid me leap, rather than marry Paris,
From off the battlements of yonder tower,
Or walk in thievish ways, or bid me lurk
Where serpents are. Chain me with roaring bears;
Or hide me nightly in a charnel-house,
O’er-cover’d quite with dead men’s rattling bones,
With reeky shanks and yellow chapless skulls.
Or bid me go into a new-made grave,
And hide me with a dead man in his shroud;
Things that, to hear them told, have made me tremble,
And I will do it without fear or doubt,
To live an unstain’d wife to my sweet love.

gemma4_gloss.en: Oh, tell me to jump instead of marrying Paris.
I could jump from the walls of that tower over there.
Or I could live like a thief.
Or I could hide where snakes are.
Chain me with roaring bears.
Or hide me every night in a house for dead bodies.
Cover me with the bones of dead men.
I would be covered in old bones and skulls.
Or tell me to go into a new grave.
Hide me with a dead man in his shroud.
These things make me tremble when I hear them.
But I will do them without fear or doubt.
I will do them to be an honest wife to my sweet love.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Hold then. Go home, be merry, give consent
To marry Paris. Wednesday is tomorrow;
Tomorrow night look that thou lie alone,
Let not thy Nurse lie with thee in thy chamber.
Take thou this vial, being then in bed,
And this distilled liquor drink thou off,
When presently through all thy veins shall run
A cold and drowsy humour; for no pulse
Shall keep his native progress, but surcease.
No warmth, no breath shall testify thou livest,
The roses in thy lips and cheeks shall fade
To paly ashes; thy eyes’ windows fall,
Like death when he shuts up the day of life.
Each part depriv’d of supple government,
Shall stiff and stark and cold appear like death.
And in this borrow’d likeness of shrunk death
Thou shalt continue two and forty hours,
And then awake as from a pleasant sleep.
Now when the bridegroom in the morning comes
To rouse thee from thy bed, there art thou dead.
Then as the manner of our country is,
In thy best robes, uncover’d, on the bier,
Thou shalt be borne to that same ancient vault
Where all the kindred of the Capulets lie.
In the meantime, against thou shalt awake,
Shall Romeo by my letters know our drift,
And hither shall he come, and he and I
Will watch thy waking, and that very night
Shall Romeo bear thee hence to Mantua.
And this shall free thee from this present shame,
If no inconstant toy nor womanish fear
Abate thy valour in the acting it.

gemma4_gloss.en: Wait then.
Go home and be happy.
Agree to marry Paris.
Wednesday is tomorrow.
Tomorrow night, make sure you lie alone.
Do not let your Nurse stay in your room with you.
Take this small bottle while you are in bed.
Drink all of this liquid.
A cold and sleepy feeling will move through your veins.
Your pulse will stop.
No warmth or breath will show that you live.
The color in your lips and cheeks will fade to gray.
Your eyes will close.
It will look like death has closed the day of life.
Every part of you will become stiff and cold.
You will look like death.
In this appearance of death, you will stay for forty-eight hours.
Then you will wake up as if from a pleasant sleep.
When the groom comes in the morning to wake you, you will appear to be dead.
Because of our local customs, you will be dressed in your best clothes.
You will be uncovered on a coffin.
You will be carried to that old vault.
All your relatives, the Capulets, lie there.
In the meantime, you will wake up.
Romeo will know our plan from my letters.
He will come here.
He and I will watch you wake up.
That same night, Romeo will take you to Mantua.
This will free you from this shame.
Unless your fear or lack of courage stops you from acting bravely.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Give me, give me! O tell not me of fear!

gemma4_gloss.en: Give it to me, give it to me!
Do not tell me about fear!

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Hold; get you gone, be strong and prosperous
In this resolve. I’ll send a friar with speed
To Mantua, with my letters to thy lord.

gemma4_gloss.en: Wait.
Go now.
Be strong and successful in this decision.
I will send a monk quickly to Mantua.
I will give him my letters for your lord.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Love give me strength, and strength shall help afford.
Farewell, dear father.

gemma4_gloss.en: Love, give me strength.
Strength will provide what I need.
Goodbye, dear father.

raw: Exeunt.
